I'm kicking off work on team workspaces for our B2B note-taking app (company stage unknown). I need a PRD that engineering and design leads will read at the kickoff meeting. They will use it to decide whether the v1 scope is clear enough to start design and engineering work, so state scope, roles and open questions precisely enough that they can challenge them.

Problem and evidence: I have no evidence to share right now: no usage data, customer quotes or research. Write the problem statement in one or two plain sentences, using only what follows from the feature itself (teams using the app have no shared workspace). Then add an "Evidence" section made of clearly marked gaps, for example "GAP: no data on how many accounts currently share notes". Do not invent statistics, quotes, customer names or customer claims anywhere in the document.

Scope for v1:
- In: creating a workspace; inviting members by email; shared notes within a workspace.
- Roles: admin and member only. Describe what each can do, and mark any permission details I haven't given as "proposed".
- Out: billing changes, SSO, guest access.
- Open question, to be left open: how existing shared notes migrate into workspaces. List it under Open Questions with the decisions it blocks, but do not propose or assume an answer.
- Cross-workspace sharing: I haven't decided whether it is in or out. Don't list it under In or Out. Put it under Open Questions as undecided.

Success metric: 20% of paid accounts create a workspace within 60 days. Give it as the primary metric, and state the definition of "paid account" and the start of the 60-day window as open items for the team to confirm. If you add any other metrics, label each one "proposed". Write no target numbers other than the 20% / 60 days I gave.

Format: use a standard PRD template with these sections: Overview and Problem, Evidence (gaps), Goals and Success Metrics, Users and Roles, Scope (In / Out), Requirements (numbered, grouped by the three in-scope capabilities), Open Questions, Risks and Dependencies, Next Steps for kickoff. Keep it to about 2 pages, so use tight bullets and short requirement lines, with no filler or generic best-practice padding.

Anything you had to assume that I haven't stated, such as a requirement detail, a permission rule or a risk, should be tagged "Assumption" in the text, so I can find and confirm it. Don't resolve anything I've left open.

Reply with the PRD only, and nothing after the final section.
